Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    cleaned = Array(rows).map do |row|
      {
        id: row[:id].presence&.to_i,
        body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      }
    end

    non_empty = cleaned.reject { |r| r[:body].empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none? { |r| r[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!

      existing_by_id = options.index_by(&:id)
      kept_ids = []

      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, index|
        pos = index + 1
        if row[:id] && existing_by_id.key?(row[:id])
          option = existing_by_id[row[:id]]
          option.update!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        else
          option = options.create!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        end
      end

      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by!(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by!(1)
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    return if position.present? || quiz.nil?

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by!(delta)
    transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      index = ordered.index { |q| q.id == id }
      return false if index.nil?

      target_index = index + delta
      return false if target_index < 0 || target_index >= ordered.size

      ordered[index], ordered[target_index] = ordered[target_index], ordered[index]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        question.update_column(:position, i + 1) if question.position != i + 1
      end
      true
    end
  end
end

Importing `@hotwired/turbo-rails` threw an uncaught `SecurityError` in `history.replaceState` when the page was opened via `http://user:pass@host/moderate`, aborting JS execution before Stimulus controllers even initialized. Since Release 1 doesn't use Turbo Drive/Streams (all interactivity is Stimulus + standard HTML forms), I'll remove `import "@hotwired/turbo-rails"` from `app/javascript/application.js` (keeping the gem & pin ready for future releases) and re-test BOTH header-based and URL-embedded Basic Auth!
steps.reasoning_content:
**A Near Miss with Basic Authentication!**

Wow, I just stumbled upon something significant! It looks like accessing a specific URL, specifically `http://confmod:talkpass!@127.0.0.1:3125/moderate/quizzes/1`, threw a *major* wrench into the works. The error message is clear: a `SecurityError` triggered by `history.replaceState` within `turbo.min.js`, stemming from the `@hotwired/turbo-rails` import in `app/javascript/application.js`.

This is *huge*! Basically, the presence of those embedded credentials in the URL is causing Turbo to crash during its initialization. This prevents Stimulus from even *starting* – so, no `question-active`, `option-rows`, or `preview`! This one edge case could have caused a significant disruption if our QA suite or any moderator authenticated via a similar URL!

The fix, thankfully, appears incredibly straightforward. It seems we don't even *need* `@hotwired/turbo-rails` on these pages at the moment. All our forms use standard HTTP methods and redirects, and we've already set `data-turbo="false"` on them. Our active toggle, option rows, and preview functionalities all rely on Stimulus. Even if we *did* want Turbo functionality in the future, reordering the imports within `application.js` (perhaps importing "controllers" first or dynamically importing Turbo based on the URL) would be more robust. However, for Release 1, we aren't utilizing Turbo Drive, Frames, or Streams *anywhere* – just Stimulus. So, the cleanest solution is to simply remove the `@hotwired/turbo-rails` import from `app/javascript/application.js` entirely. This eliminates the crash and should speed up page loads without any Turbo interference.

Now, let's also investigate how the `fetch()` API behaves in Chromium when Basic Authentication is involved. We'll remove the `@hotwired/turbo-rails` import and re-test, to see if `fetch()` is also affected.

steps.message: WHAT A CATCH! In Chromium, `fetch(relativePath)` resolves against `document.baseURI` which includes embedded `user:pass@` credentials when opened via URL-embedded Basic Auth, causing Fetch to reject with `TypeError: Request cannot be constructed from a URL that includes credentials`. Resolving against `window.location.origin` strips credentials cleanly while keeping `credentials: "same-origin"` working! Let's fix `question_active_controller.js` and verify!
steps.reasoning_content:
**The Authentication Bug - A Deep Dive**

Whoa, hold on a second! This is crucial. I need to take a closer look at this unexpected behavior, even without Turbo enabled, where toggling the active state of a question still leaves "1 of 1 question active." It's Chromium-specific, and I think I've figured out why.

The problem lies with how the `fetch` API is resolving the URL in the `question_active_controller.js`. When a page loads, say from `http://confmod:talkpass!@127.0.0.1:3125/moderate/quizzes/1`, a `fetch("/moderate/quizzes/1/questions/1/toggle_active")` call is, incredibly, resolving against `document.baseURI`. This includes the username and password! Consequently, the `fetch` call will reject with a `TypeError: Request cannot be constructed from a URL that includes credentials`, which we're catching and silently reverting. No wonder our state wasn't updating correctly.

To verify, let's look at the fetch spec. It states that `fetch(relativeUrl)` resolves `relativeUrl` against `document.baseURI`. Since our `document.baseURI` is the URL that has credentials, the URL we're constructing includes those credentials.

In contrast, consider this alternative: `new URL(form.getAttribute("action"), window.location.origin).href`. This will construct the correct URL without including credentials, because `window.location.origin` *never* contains a username or password. This is a brilliant find.

This is an insane, but incredible catch! Let's examine the difference between `window.location.href` and `window.location.origin`:

*   `window.location.href` is `"http://confmod:talkpass!@127.0.0.1:3125/moderate/quizzes/1"` (credentials included).
*   `window.location.origin` is `"http://127.0.0.1:3125"` (no credentials).

Therefore, when we use `new URL(form.getAttribute("action"), window.location.origin).href`, we're getting `"http://127.0.0.1:3125/moderate/quizzes/1/questions/1/toggle_active"`. This avoids the credentials, so `fetch()` succeeds, and Chromium can then send our cached Basic Auth credentials via `credentials: "same-origin"`.

The solution is to update `question_active_controller.js` to use `new URL(form.getAttribute("action"), window.location.origin).href`! I'm going to test it right away.

import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["item", "number", "summary"]

  connect() {
    this.queue = Promise.resolve()
  }

  toggle(event) {
    const checkbox = event.currentTarget
    const form = checkbox.closest("form")
    const item = checkbox.closest("[data-question-active-target='item']")
    const active = checkbox.checked
    const csrfToken = document.querySelector("meta[name='csrf-token']")?.content
    const url = new URL(form.getAttribute("action"), window.location.origin).href

    this.queue = this.queue
      .then(() =>
        fetch(url, {
          method: "PATCH",
          headers: {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Accept": "application/json",
            "X-CSRF-Token": csrfToken || ""
          },
          credentials: "same-origin",
          keepalive: true,
          body: JSON.stringify({ question: { active } })
        }).then((response) => {
          if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`)
          if (item) {
            item.classList.toggle("question-item--inactive", !active)
          }
          this.updateNumbersAndSummary()
        })
      )
      .catch(() => {
        checkbox.checked = !active
        if (item) {
          item.classList.toggle("question-item--inactive", active)
        }
        this.updateNumbersAndSummary()
      })
  }

  updateNumbersAndSummary() {
    let activeCount = 0
    const totalCount = this.itemTargets.length

    this.itemTargets.forEach((item, idx) => {
      const checkbox = item.querySelector("input[type='checkbox'][name='question[active]']")
      const isActive = checkbox ? checkbox.checked : false
      const numberEl = this.numberTargets[idx]
      if (isActive) {
        activeCount += 1
        if (numberEl) numberEl.textContent = String(activeCount)
      } else {
        if (numberEl) numberEl.textContent = "—"
      }
    })

    if (this.hasSummaryTarget) {
      const noun = totalCount === 1 ? "question" : "questions"
      this.summaryTarget.textContent = `${activeCount} of ${totalCount} ${noun} active`
    }
  }
}
EOF

# Quizzy Architecture Notes (Release 1: Moderator Quiz Preparation)

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, and Stimulus. All CSS, JS, and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required).

Future live-quiz releases can build `runs` / `participants` / `answers` referencing `quizzes`, `questions`, and `options` directly; option updates preserve existing `option.id` values when edited in place.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Missing or wrong credentials return `401 Unauthorized`.
- `GET /up` (health check) and `GET /` (landing page) do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- `question_active_controller.js` resolves PATCH URLs against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so `fetch()` works reliably under both `Authorization` header auth and URL-embedded Basic Auth, with queued requests and `keepalive: true`.
- `option_rows_controller.js` dynamically adds/removes option rows and renumbers labels (`Option N`, `Option N is correct`) cleanly.
- `preview_controller.js` runs preview entirely in memory (no DB/session/storage writes), stepping through active questions in order and resetting cleanly on "Start over" or reload.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`).
EOF
